title: LISD Hands Out New Coats to More Than 400 Elementary Students
excerpt: More than 400 LISD elementary students received brand-new coats at the district's 17th annual “Coat Them with Love” distribution at the Rafael Martinez Conference Center, with pizza, coloring books and letters to Santa rounding out the morning.
content:
Christmas came early for hundreds of Laredo Independent School District elementary students, who received brand-new coats at the district’s 17th annual “Coat Them with Love” distribution event, the district announced.

More than 400 elementary students filled the Rafael Martinez Conference Center for the giveaway, run by the district’s Office of Communications. Board President Veronica Orduno and Trustee Monica Garcia joined district staff and central office administrators in handing each student a new jacket, according to the district.

Each student also received a coloring book and was treated to pizza and punch, and children had the chance to write a letter to Santa and drop it in Santa’s special mailbox, the district said.

Members of the Superintendent’s Student Advisory Council volunteered at the distribution on Monday morning, helping younger students write their Santa letters and color, and handing out coats, before meeting with Superintendent Guillermo Pro, according to the district.

“This is one of the events that we all look forward to in our office every year,” said Bobby Trevino, LISD public information coordinator. “When the kids put on their new jackets, those looks and smiles, that is what it’s all about.”

The coats were bought with proceeds from the district’s annual BOWL 4 KIDS bowling competition at Jett Bowl, where close to 200 LISD employees and community partners bowled to raise the money, the district said. Community partners included Laredo Federal Credit Union, KMP Law, PNC Bank, the Juan Cruz Law Firm, Falcon Bank, Clear Choice ER, AFLAC, Whataburger and Sunbelt Air.

Over the last 17 years, the Coat Them with Love campaign has provided more than 7,000 coats to LISD students, according to the district. Anyone interested in donating new coats can contact the LISD Office of Communications at 273-1730.

Sources: Laredo Independent School District, Nov. 19, 2026.
